title_en: China Railway 22nd Bureau Group Fourth Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Ruixun Traffic Development Co., Ltd. and Anhui Expressway Holding Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 3 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues concerning the Priority Right to Compensation for Construction Project Price provides: 'The construction project price includes the actual expenses incurred by the contractor for the project, such as remuneration for workers and material costs, but does not include losses caused by the employer's breach of contract.' The losses from work stoppage and suspension and losses from material price differences caused by the employer's breach of contract as claimed by the contractor in the lawsuit do not fall within the scope of the priority right to compensation for construction project price. Where the contractor requests the exercise of the priority right to compensation for the above two types of amounts, the people's court shall not support such request.

full_text_en:
China Railway 22nd Bureau Group Fourth Engineering Co., Ltd. v. Anhui Ruixun Transportation Development Co., Ltd. and Anhui Expressway Holding Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over a construction project contract

【Ruling Summary】

Article 3 of the Reply of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Priority of Compensation for Construction Project Price provides: "The construction project price includes the contractor's actual expenses such as remuneration for workers to be paid and material costs for the construction project, but does not include losses caused by the employer's breach of contract." The losses from work stoppages and slowdowns and losses from material price differences claimed by the contractor in the litigation, which are caused by the employer's breach of contract, do not fall within the scope of the right to priority of compensation for construction project price. Where the contractor requests to exercise the right of priority for the above two categories of amounts, the people's court shall not support such request.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2014) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 56

Appellant (plaintiff at first instance): China Railway 22nd Bureau Group Fourth Engineering Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 39 Heping Road, Gaobeidian City, Hebei Province.

Legal representative: Yang Zhongxiao, chairman of the board.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Anhong, male, Han ethnicity, born on April 27, 1975, project manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Yong, lawyer of Beijing Tongchuang Law Firm.

Appellant (defendant at first instance): Anhui Ruixun Transportation Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at Ziyun Road (within the Private Science and Technology Economic Park), Economic and Technological Development Zone, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Legal representative: Liu Feng, general manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Wang Wenfeng, lawyer of Anhui Chengyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Xiangyu, lawyer of Beijing Juntai Law Firm.

Respondent (defendant at first instance): Anhui Expressway Holding Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 520 Wangjiang West Road, High-tech Development Zone, Hefei City, Anhui Province.

Legal representative: Zhou Renqiang, chairman of the board.

Agent ad litem: Song Shijun, lawyer of Anhui Antaida Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Cheng Jun, lawyer of Anhui Antaida Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a construction project contract between the appellant China Railway 22nd Bureau Group Fourth Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Railway Company) and the appellant Anhui Ruixun Transportation Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ruixun Company) and the respondent Anhui Expressway Holding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Anhui Expressway Company), the Anhui High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) rendered the Civil Judgment (2011) Wan Min Si Chu Zi No. 8 on October 16, 2013. China Railway Company and Ruixun Company, not satisfied with the judgment, appealed to this court. This court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a hearing of this case on March 31, 2014. The agents ad litem of Ruixun Company, Wang Wenfeng and Zhang Xiangyu, the agents ad litem of China Railway Company, Zhang Anhong and Li Yong, and the agents ad litem of Anhui Expressway Company, Song Shijun and Cheng Jun, appeared before the court and participated in the proceedings. This case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found through trial: In 2003, Anhui Ruixin Transportation Development Co., Ltd. (later renamed as Ruixun Company, hereinafter collectively referred to as Ruixun Company) obtained the construction and operation right of the Fuyang to Zhouji Expressway (hereinafter referred to as the Fuzhou Expressway). On December 31 of the same year, China Railway 18th Bureau Group Fourth Engineering Co., Ltd. (later renamed as China Railway Company, hereinafter collectively referred to as China Railway Company), after undergoing the bidding process, signed a Contract Agreement with Ruixun Company for the subgrade construction of the Fuzhou Expressway, agreeing that Ruixun Company would contract out Section 13 of the Fuzhou Expressway to China Railway Company for construction, with a total contract price of RMB 201,901,950 and a construction period of 22 months, among other terms.

On February 18, 2004, the General Chief Engineer's Office of the Fuzhou Expressway Subgrade Project of Anhui Provincial Highway Engineering Construction Supervision Co., Ltd. issued a Commencement Order to contractors of various sections including China Railway Company, specifying that the construction period would be calculated from February 18, 2004. China Railway Company carried out the construction in accordance with the contract, but failed to complete the works within the contractually agreed construction period. China Railway Company completed in March 2006 the construction quantities that were originally scheduled to be completed by March 2005.

On December 22, 2008, the Anhui Provincial People's Government (hereinafter referred to as the Anhui Provincial Government) convened a coordination meeting on the resumption of construction of the Fuzhou Expressway, which resulted in the formation of Anhui Provincial Government Special Meeting Minutes No. 253 (hereinafter referred to as the No. 253 Meeting Minutes). The main contents were as follows: It was decided that the Department of Transport of Anhui Province (hereinafter referred to as the Anhui Provincial Transport Department) would take back the construction and operation right of the Fuzhou Expressway and hand it over to Anhui Expressway Company as the new project owner to be responsible for construction and operation. Anhui Expressway Company, as the new project owner, would bear the responsibility for organizing and coordinating new construction units to resume work, while the original project owner, Ruixun Company, would bear the responsibility for dealing with the original construction units and handling the project's pre-existing creditor's rights and debts. Ruixun Company was required to properly handle the creditor's rights and debts and interest relationships with the original construction units, supervision units, etc., and actively raise funds to pay off outstanding debts, material costs, wages of migrant workers, etc. For the completed works that had been audited and measured, where the Anhui Provincial Transport Department, Anhui Expressway Company, and Ruixun Company had consistent understanding and signed clear opinions, the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Anhui Province (hereinafter referred to as the Anhui SASAC) would strictly review and verify in accordance with regulations and promptly report to the Anhui Provincial Government for study; for completed works that had not been measured or had been measured but with inconsistent understanding, the Anhui SASAC would coordinate with the parties as soon as possible to reach consensus.

On April 1, 2009, Ruixun Company and China Railway Company signed an Agreement, stipulating: 1. Both parties jointly confirmed that Ruixun Company still owed China Railway Company a total of RMB 391,674.41 for completed and measured works. After deducting the reduced amount of RMB 1,458,466 for completed and measured works that should be borne by China Railway Company, China Railway Company still needed to refund Ruixun Company the overpaid amount of RMB 1,066,791.59 for completed and measured works. 2. Both parties jointly verified that the amount of China Railway Company's completed but unmeasured works totaled RMB 6,410,929.13; if the audit firm commissioned by the Anhui SASAC reasonably reduced the above works amount based on sufficient grounds, both parties agreed to be bound by the final amount determined by the audit unit, provided that Ruixun Company, during the period when the audit unit solicits opinions from the audited entity, must timely notify China Railway Company to raise objections or submit written objections and reasons with the audit unit regarding the basis for reducing China Railway Company's completed but unmeasured works; otherwise, any reduction of China Railway Company's above works amount by the audit unit would be entirely borne by Ruixun Company. 3. Both parties jointly confirmed that the warranty deposit paid by China Railway Company to Ruixun Company was RMB 7,462,567.99, and Ruixun Company agreed to refund it in full. Both parties agreed to commence negotiations on the claim matters before April 20, 2009, etc. Thereafter, Ruixun Company paid part of the project price to China Railway Company.

On May 22, 2009, China Railway Company submitted a written appeal to Ruixun Company and Wanrui Audit Firm, the audit unit for the project involved, stating that China Railway Company was shocked upon receiving the electronic document from Ruixun Company regarding the preliminary results of the second-step audit of the Fuzhou Expressway project at 10:00 a.m. on May 21, 2009, and could not understand or accept the reduction of the completed but unmeasured works amounts, and therefore filed an appeal, among other things.

During the first-instance litigation, to prove its claims, China Railway Company submitted to the court of first instance the daily statistics sheets on idle personnel and machinery due to work stoppages and slowdowns signed by Wang Bo, the on-site supervisor, for the period from March 2004 to March 2005, and the monthly statistics sheets on costs of idle personnel and machinery. The daily statistics sheets indicated that the reasons for the work stoppages and slowdowns were insufficient funds and unresolved issues with the borrow pit.

During the first-instance litigation, at the request of China Railway Company, the court of first instance lawfully commissioned Anhui Pearl Construction Project Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Pearl Company) to conduct an appraisal on whether the losses from work stoppages and slowdowns claimed by China Railway Company existed and, if so, the specific amount. On July 17, 2012, Pearl Company issued the Appraisal Report on the Cost Losses from Work Stoppages and Slowdowns for Section 13 of Fuzhou Expressway, Wan Mingzhu Ji Zi (2012) No. 119 (hereinafter referred to as the Appraisal Report), concluding that, based on the available materials, the losses from work stoppages and slowdowns for Section 13 of the Fuzhou Expressway undertaken by China Railway Company were as follows: 1. Losses from work stoppages and slowdowns during the first suspension period from March 2004 to March 2005: (1) Determined portion: RMB 6,778,661.54; (2) Uncertain portion: RMB 6,929,833.87. 2. For losses from work stoppages and slowdowns during the second suspension period from November 2006 to March 2009, the specific amount could not be calculated based on the available evidence. On March 7, 2013, Pearl Company issued a Supplemental Appraisal Report, concluding that, based on the available materials, the costs incurred by China Railway Company due to the increase in prices of raw materials and oil products resulting from the 2004 work stoppage were RMB 3,119,237.63.

China Railway Company filed a lawsuit, requesting: 1. That Ruixun Company pay the outstanding project price of RMB 5,585,903.73, plus interest losses calculated from June 1, 2009, to the date of actual payment (at the contemporaneous loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China); 2. Compensation for interest losses of RMB 201,018.62 arising from the delayed payment of the advance payment for commencement; 3. Compensation for losses from work stoppages and slowdowns during the first suspension period from January 2004 to March 2005 in the amount of RMB 22,565,873.85; compensation for losses from work stoppages and slowdowns during the second suspension period from November 2006 to April 2009 in the amount of RMB 32,006,719.12 (rent of RMB 40,986.67 + land use fee of RMB 405,096 + losses from idle personnel and machinery of RMB 30,970,300 + lime payment of RMB 590,336.45); compensation for the increased management fee of RMB 4,078,795 arising from the extension of the construction period and the reduction of the total actual project price; 4. Confirmation that China Railway Company has a priority right to compensation with respect to the claimed project price and various loss amounts against the project involved; 5. That Anhui Expressway Company bear joint and several liability for payment.

The court of first instance held that the Contract Agreement and the Agreement were legally valid. China Railway Company's claim for payment of the outstanding project price and interest by Ruixun Company lacked factual basis and was not supported. China Railway Company's claim for interest losses due to delayed payment of the advance payment for commencement was not supported. The determined portion of RMB 6,778,661.54 in the losses from work stoppages and slowdowns claimed by China Railway Company for the period from March 2004 to March 2005 was supported; the uncertain portion was not supported. China Railway Company's claimed losses from work stoppages and slowdowns for the period from November 2006 to April 2009 were not supported. With respect to the increased costs of raw materials and oil products during the work stoppage and slowdown period, Ruixun Company and China Railway Company were to bear them equally, and Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company RMB 1,559,618.82. China Railway Company's claims for management fees, for confirmation of the priority right to compensation with respect to the project involved, and for Anhui Expressway Company to bear joint and several liability were all not supported. Accordingly, the court of first instance rendered the judgment: 1. Ruixun Company shall compensate China Railway Company for economic losses of RMB 8,338,280.36 within ten days after the judgment takes effect; 2. All other claims of China Railway Company are dismissed. If the obligation to pay a sum of money is not performed within the period specified in the judgment, the interest on the debt for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC. Court acceptance fee of RMB 346,810.65, with China Railway Company bearing RMB 299,405.65 and Ruixun Company bearing RMB 47,405; appraisal fee of RMB 350,000, with China Railway Company bearing RMB 297,940 and Ruixun Company bearing RMB 52,060.

Ruixun Company appealed, arguing: 1. The statistics sheets signed by Wang Bo, on which the first-instance judgment based its finding of work stoppages, are in contradiction with other evidence and were issued unlawfully, and therefore cannot be used as the basis for deciding the case. Ruixun Company has proven that the project involved was not suspended during 2004 and 2005, and there were no losses from work stoppages; the first-instance judgment's finding that such losses existed during that period is erroneous in fact. 2. The first-instance judgment, relying on the Appraisal Report, ordered both parties to share the losses from the increase in oil product prices, which is contrary to the facts and the principle of fairness.

China Railway Company appealed and responded, arguing: 1. With respect to the audited reduction amount of RMB 2,573,395.71 for completed but unmeasured works and the unmeasured project price of RMB 1,378,989.97 not included in the audit, given that these quantities of works indeed exist and Ruixun Company fully acknowledges them, the settlement should be based on the actual situation. Moreover, Ruixun Company failed to timely notify the audit unit of the audit status, so Ruixun Company should pay the reduced amount and the outstanding project price for the unaudited works totaling RMB 3,816,805.76, along with the corresponding interest calculated from June 1, 2009. 2. According to the Agreement, the second installment of the advance payment for commencement should have been paid when the Commencement Order was issued on February 18, 2004, but Ruixun Company delayed payment until November 28, 2004, a delay of nine months and ten days. Ruixun Company should pay interest of RMB 201,018.62 on the advance payment of RMB 5,047,548 for the nine-month period at the contemporaneous loan interest rate. 3. The court of first instance, on the one hand, acknowledged the authenticity and validity of the Statistics Sheets on Work Stoppages and Slowdowns signed by Wang Bo, but on the other hand, only supported the losses of RMB 6,778,661.54 for the suspension period from July to November 2004, and refused to support the losses of RMB 6,929,833.87 for the periods of March to June 2004, December 2004, and January to March 2005, citing "contradictions" in the statistics sheets, which is without factual and legal basis. As for the second suspension losses from November 2006 to April 2009, although there is no signature confirmation from the supervisor, the fact of work stoppage is undeniable, and the reasons for the stoppage are very clear. Considering that the evidence for the claimed second suspension losses of RMB 22 million in the first-instance complaint was insufficient, on appeal, China Railway Company only requests a discretionary award of RMB 4 million. 4. The 2004 work stoppage was entirely caused by Ruixun Company's insufficient funds. Ruixun Company should bear full responsibility for the increased costs of raw materials and oil products resulting from the work stoppage. The first-instance judgment's decision that each party bears 50% is not in line with the facts. 5. Clauses 51.1 and 52.3 of the Bidding Documents provide that if the total increase or decrease in the contract price exceeds 15% of the effective contract price, a management fee adjustment shall be made. If positive, the management fee is adjusted downward; if negative, it is adjusted upward. The contract price was RMB 201.9 million, but the actual construction value was RMB 116.2 million, a reduction of nearly half, far exceeding the 15% threshold. According to the above contract terms, the management fee needs to be adjusted upward. 6. To protect the interests of the vast number of migrant workers, at a minimum, the priority right to compensation for construction project price should be confirmed with respect to the outstanding project price, costs of personnel and machinery, increased material costs, and management fees. 7. The Anhui Provincial Government took back the Fuzhou Expressway and handed it over to Anhui Expressway Company for operation, and required Ruixun Company to transfer the outstanding issues to the relevant government departments and Anhui Expressway Company for handling. Therefore, Anhui Expressway Company should bear joint and several liability for clearing the debts owed by Ruixun Company. In conclusion, China Railway Company requests that Ruixun Company's appeal be dismissed and that the judgment be modified as follows: 1. Set aside item 2 of the first-instance judgment, and instead order Ruixun Company to pay the outstanding project price of RMB 3,816,805.76 and interest losses of RMB 287,119.21 (calculated provisionally up to October 30, 2010) from June 1, 2009, to the effective date of the judgment, pay interest of RMB 201,018.62 for the delayed payment of the advance payment for commencement, pay losses from work stoppages and slowdowns of RMB 6,929,833.87 for the first suspension period from March 2004 to March 2005 and RMB 4,000,000 for the second suspension period from November 2006 to April 2009, pay RMB 1,559,618.82 for losses due to price differences in raw materials and oil products, and pay RMB 4,078,795 for the increased management fee due to the extension of the construction period and the reduction of the total actual project price; 2. Confirm that China Railway Company has a priority right to compensation for the project price with respect to the project involved; 3. Anhui Expressway Company shall bear joint and several liability for payment.

Ruixun Company responded to China Railway Company's appeal, arguing: 1. With respect to the completed but unmeasured works, the parties clearly agreed to submit them to the audit unit for review. The amount approved by the audit unit and the approval procedure were not improper, and Ruixun Company has timely performed its obligation to notify China Railway Company in accordance with the agreement. Therefore, the cost of this part should be based on the audit unit's opinion, and Ruixun Company no longer owes China Railway Company any project price or interest. 2. Regarding the delayed payment of the project price, the court of first instance found the facts clearly. China Railway Company did not provide evidence to prove that Ruixun Company delayed payment of the project price, and its appellate request is without basis. 3. Regarding the losses from work stoppages and slowdowns, the signature of supervisor Wang Bo is invalid and was Wang Bo's personal act. The Appraisal Report, which bases its findings on invalid signatures, has no basis. Furthermore, China Railway Company has not provided evidence that it actually incurred the claimed losses from work stoppages and slowdowns, indicating that it suffered no losses at all. Moreover, even if there were work stoppages and slowdowns, they were caused by China Railway Company's own reasons. The first-instance judgment's decision to award the first suspension losses is baseless, and Ruixun Company has already filed an appeal requesting support for its position. 4. Regarding the issue of losses from material price differences due to the 2004 to 2005 work stoppage, China Railway Company did not provide evidence to prove that it actually incurred the cost difference. Furthermore, the delay in the project was caused by China Railway Company's poor organization. If such price difference losses existed, they should be borne by China Railway Company, not shared by Ruixun Company. 5. Regarding China Railway Company's claim for management fees, China Railway Company has no evidence to prove that such fees were actually incurred, and such fees have already been compensated through the actual idling losses. China Railway Company's claim constitutes a duplicate claim. 6. China Railway Company's claim for priority rights to compensation with respect to the construction project involved does not meet the statutory prerequisites. On the one hand, the construction project is a public welfare infrastructure that is not suitable for appraisal or auction. On the other hand, the construction contract between Ruixun Company and China Railway Company has already been terminated, and China Railway Company has not asserted its priority right, thereby waiving that right. In conclusion, Ruixun Company requests that China Railway Company's appeal against Ruixun Company be dismissed and that its own appeal be upheld.

Anhui Expressway Company, in its defense against China Railway Company's appeal, argued that it agreed with Ruixun Company's defense that the claims for project payment and various losses should not be upheld. Regarding China Railway Company's claim for a right to priority of payment for the project in question, on the one hand, the project in question was a public facility and was not suitable for discount or auction; on the other hand, China Railway Company's claim in this action was for losses caused by breach of contract, which did not constitute expenses actually incurred such as staff remuneration or material costs, and also did not satisfy the conditions set forth in Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's "Reply on Issues Concerning the Right to Priority of Payment for Construction Project Price," and therefore China Railway Company's claim should be dismissed. With respect to China Railway Company's demand that Anhui Expressway Company bear joint and several liability, the documents of the Anhui Provincial Government and the Anhui Provincial Department of Transportation both clearly stated that the original debts and claims of the project in question were to be handled by Ruixun Company, and never required Anhui Expressway Company to assume joint and several payment liability. Moreover, Ruixun Company was a legal person with civil capacity for rights and conduct. China Railway Company's allegation that Ruixun Company was insolvent had no legal basis, and therefore its appeal requesting Anhui Expressway Company to bear joint and several liability had no factual or legal basis. In summary, the request to dismiss China Railway Company's appeal against Anhui Expressway Company was made.

This court, upon trial, finds that the "Agreement" signed between Ruixun Company and China Railway Company stipulated that the special terms of the contract, the general terms of the contract, the special terms of the technical specifications, the bid, and the appendix to the bid, etc., were integral parts of the agreement, and the documents complemented each other.

Regarding the amendment of the contract, Article 52.3 of the General Terms of the Contract stipulated that if, at the time of issuing the completion certificate, it was discovered that the total increase or decrease in the contract price exceeded 15% of the "effective contract price" (where "effective contract price" refers to the contract price after deducting provisional sums), such total excess or reduction of 15% or more arose from: (1) the cumulative result of all variations valued under Articles 52.1 and 52.2; and (2) all adjustments made to the estimated quantities in the bill of quantities based on actual measurements, excluding provisional sums and price adjustments for price factors. If this occurred, the supervising engineer should, after consultation with the employer and the contractor, determine an adjustment amount for management fees, to be deducted from or added to the contract price.

Regarding the claims procedure, Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract stipulated that if the contractor made a claim for any additional payment under any clause of the contract, it should submit its notice of intention to claim to the supervising engineer within 21 days of the first occurrence of the event giving rise to the claim, with a copy to the employer. Upon receiving such notice of intention to claim, the supervising engineer, without needing to confirm whether it was the employer's responsibility, should first examine the records made at the time and could instruct the contractor to further prepare records made at the time. If the claim submitted by the contractor failed to comply with the provisions of this clause, the contractor was not entitled to the claim or was entitled only to that portion of the claim verified by the supervising engineer based on the records made at the time. After consultation with the employer and the contractor, the supervising engineer determined the full or partial amount of the claim to which the contractor was entitled. The Special Terms of the Contract further added to Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract, stipulating that the records submitted by the contractor in support of the claim included records of conversations between the employer, the supervising engineer, and the contractor; statistical reports on labor, materials, and machinery at the site; construction memoranda; supervision records; and various forms filled out by the site supervising engineer.

Regarding the employer's liability for breach of contract, Article 69.1 of the General Terms of the Contract stipulated that if, within 42 days after the payment period specified in Article 60.15, the employer failed to pay the contractor the amount payable under any payment certificate issued by the supervising engineer, without providing reasons to the contractor; or unreasonably obstructed or refused to grant the necessary approval for the issuance of any such certificate under any provision of the contract, the contractor was entitled to terminate its undertaking under the contract, and upon notice to the employer, with a copy to the supervising engineer, such termination would take effect 14 days after the notice was given. Article 69.4 stipulated that after the occurrence of the employer's breach as described in Article 69.1(1), the contractor could give 28 days' notice to the employer, with a copy to the supervising engineer, indicating that the contractor might suspend the work under the contract or reduce the rate of progress. Such action by the contractor did not affect its right to receive interest and to terminate the contract. If, after giving 28 days' notice to the employer, the contractor suspended work or reduced the rate of progress in accordance with this clause, and thereby suffered delay or incurred additional costs, the supervising engineer should, after consultation with the contractor and the employer, determine: (1) the extension of time to which the contractor was entitled; and (2) the amount of such costs to be added to the contract price.

Regarding variations in costs, Article 70.3 of the General Terms of the Contract stipulated that if the contractor failed to complete the works under the contract within the time stated in the appendix to the bid, then for the works constructed after the date of completion, the price adjustment calculation should use the price index for the year in which such date of completion fell as the current price index. However, for works constructed after the extended date of completion had expired, the price adjustment calculation should use the price index for the year in which such extended date of completion fell as the current price index.

It was further found that the "Appraisal Report" stated that the determined portion of the cost during the first period of work stoppage and idling from 2004 to 2005 was RMB 6,778,661.54, which referred to the specific daily statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature, as well as the monthly statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature. For the uncertain portion of the cost of RMB 6,929,833.87, this referred to: for December 2004, the specific daily statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature only had details from December 1 to 6, with no details for other days; for January-June 2004 and January-March 2005, there were only monthly statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature, without the corresponding daily statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature. Both China Railway Company and Ruixun Company acknowledged the facts recorded above.

Document No. (Fuzhou Zongjianban [2004] 011) of the General Supervising Engineer's Office for the Fuzhou Expressway Subgrade Project in Anhui Province stated that upon review, all construction units had problems with insufficient and mismatched machinery and equipment. Notice No. 2004-56 of the Engineering Supervision Notice for the Fuzhou Expressway Subgrade Project stated that Zhang Moumou of the No. 13 Contract Project Department was absent from the site from October 22 to November 14 without going through the leave procedures, and was fined RMB 40,000 as a punishment. It was hoped that the No. 13 Contract Project Department would strictly implement the project management system and not repeat the offense. The above documents and notices were provided by China Railway Company itself as evidence.

For the losses due to work stoppage and idling during the period from November 2006 to April 2009, China Railway Company also admitted in the proceedings before this court that it had not made a claim in accordance with the contract, and in its appeal, it only requested the court to determine that Ruixun Company compensate it RMB 4 million for such losses.

On December 24, 2008, the "Memorandum" signed between Ruixun Company and China Railway Company stated that with respect to China Railway Company's request for payment of RMB 4,078,795 for increased management fees due to the extension of the construction period and the reduction of the total actual project price, this was a matter of disagreement between the parties, and Ruixun Company indicated that this fee would be handled as a claim matter.

It was further found that on June 25, 2009, the Anhui Provincial Department of Transportation issued an "Opinion on the First Distribution of Compensation for the Repurchase of the Right to Operate the Fuzhou Expressway," which stated that the first installment of RMB 1.55 billion for the compensation for the repurchase of the right to operate the Fuzhou Expressway would be used first to pay RMB 200 million of Ruixun Company's outstanding local and construction project payments, and the remaining RMB 1.35 billion would be used to repay the principal and interest of loans from Industrial and Commercial Bank of China and Bank of China in accordance with the principle of proportional repayment.

On December 16, 2010, this court issued Enforcement Ruling No. (2010) Zhi Fu Zi 19, which stated that Anhui Expressway Company's obligation was to assist in ceasing payment of the matured debt of RMB 30 million owed to Ruixun Company, and not that Anhui Expressway Company should assume Ruixun Company's debts arising from the project in question.

The other facts found by this court upon trial are the same as those found by the trial court.

This court holds that, in light of the parties' pleadings, the disputes between the parties in this case are as follows: (1) whether China Railway Company's claim for Ruixun Company to pay project payment of RMB 3,816,805.76 and corresponding interest is established; (2) whether Ruixun Company was in delay in paying the advance payment for the project and whether it should compensate China Railway Company for the interest of RMB 201,018.62 on the delayed advance payment; (3) whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for losses due to work stoppage and idling, and if so, the amount of compensation; (4) whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for the price difference loss on raw materials and fuel oil caused by the work stoppage from March 2004 to March 2005, and if so, the amount of compensation; (5) whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for the management fee of RMB 4,078,795; (6) whether Anhui Expressway Company should bear joint and several liability for the amounts payable by Ruixun Company to China Railway Company; (7) whether China Railway Company's claim for a right to priority of payment for the project in question can be established. This court analyzes and determines the above disputes as follows:

(1) On the issue of whether China Railway Company's claim for Ruixun Company to pay project payment of RMB 3,816,805.76 and corresponding interest is established.

On May 22, 2009, China Railway Company stated in its petition letter that it received an electronic document from Ruixun Company regarding the preliminary audit results of the Fuzhou Expressway project at 10:00 a.m. on May 21, 2009. From this, it can be confirmed that with regard to the audit of the completed but unmeasured portions under the "Agreement," Ruixun Company had timely notified China Railway Company; otherwise, China Railway Company would not have been able to submit its petition opinion on the above audit results. Therefore, China Railway Company's ground of appeal that Ruixun Company failed to fulfill its obligation to timely notify the audit results is clearly contradictory to the facts it admitted. This court does not accept this ground of appeal.

Furthermore, with respect to China Railway Company's allegation that the audit unit commissioned by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Anhui Province had no reason for not including RMB 1,378,989.97 in the audit of the completed but unmeasured portions and for reducing RMB 2,573,395.71, according to the "Agreement" signed between Ruixun Company and China Railway Company on April 1, 2009, for the project payment of RMB 6,410,929.13 for the completed but unmeasured portions, if the audit firm commissioned by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Anhui Province reasonably reduced the above quantities based on sufficient reasons, both parties agreed to take the final amount determined by the audit unit as the standard. Under the circumstance that Ruixun Company had timely notified China Railway Company of the audit results in accordance with the agreement, then according to the above agreement, if China Railway Company could not raise a reasonable objection to the above reduction results, it should settle the project payment between China Railway Company and Ruixun Company based on the audit results of the audit unit. From the facts of this case, although China Railway Company claimed that it had objected to the audit results, it did not provide evidence to prove that the audit unit's reduction was erroneous, and until the trial of this case by this court, China Railway Company still failed to provide evidence to prove that the audit unit's reduction results were erroneous. Therefore, the trial court's settlement of the project payment for the completed but unmeasured portions of the project in question based on the audit unit's reduction results was consistent with the agreement between Ruixun Company and China Railway Company and was well-founded. China Railway Company's appeal request regarding the RMB 1,378,989.97 not included in the audit and the RMB 2,573,395.71 reduction by the audit unit has no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

(2) On the issue of whether Ruixun Company was in delay in paying the advance payment for the project and whether it should compensate China Railway Company for the interest of RMB 201,018.62 on the delayed advance payment.

On the one hand, during the litigation of this case, China Railway Company did not provide evidence to prove that Ruixun Company was in breach of contract by delaying the payment of the advance payment for the project. Therefore, it is impossible to determine the exact time and amount of the delay in paying the commencement advance payment, and also impossible to calculate the interest on the delayed payment. On the other hand, even if there was a situation where Ruixun Company breached the contract by delaying the payment of the advance payment, China Railway Company's request for Ruixun Company to pay interest on the delayed advance payment cannot be upheld. The main reasons are as follows: First, according to Article 69.1 of the General Terms of the Contract, if Ruixun Company was in delay in paying the project payment, China Railway Company was entitled to terminate its undertaking under the contract, with notice to the employer and a copy to the supervising engineer. However, from the actual performance of the construction contract in this case, China Railway Company did not terminate the contract in accordance with the above provision, nor did it fulfill the obligation of giving notice to the employer and copying the supervising engineer. This should be regarded as its implied consent to Ruixun Company's delay in paying the project advance payment. Second, even if Ruixun Company was in delay in paying the project advance payment and had the obligation to pay China Railway Company delayed interest under the General Terms of the Contract, China Railway Company should also, in accordance with Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract, submit its notice of intention to claim to the supervising engineer within 21 days of the first occurrence of the event giving rise to the claim, with a copy to the employer. However, China Railway Company did not provide evidence to prove that, in accordance with the above provision, it had submitted a claim for interest on the delayed advance payment to Ruixun Company. Therefore, according to the provision of that article that "if the claim submitted by the contractor fails to comply with the provisions of this clause, the contractor is not entitled to the claim," China Railway Company is also not entitled to compensation for this portion of interest.

In summary, the trial court's dismissal of China Railway Company's request for Ruixun Company to pay interest of RMB 201,018.62 on the delayed advance payment, under the circumstances where the interest on the delayed payment could not be calculated and China Railway Company failed to provide evidence that it had timely submitted a claim to Ruixun Company after the loss occurred, was not improper. China Railway Company's appeal request for the interest on the project advance payment has no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

(3) On the issue of whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for losses due to work stoppage and idling, and if so, the amount of compensation.

For this disputed issue, the pleadings of China Railway Company and Ruixun Company include the following two parts of losses due to work stoppage and idling:

1. On the issue of losses due to work stoppage and idling during the period from March 2004 to March 2005. According to Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract, if the contractor makes a claim for any additional payment under any clause of the contract, it should submit its notice of intention to claim to the supervising engineer within 21 days of the first occurrence of the event giving rise to the claim, with a copy to the employer. After consultation with the employer and the contractor, the supervising engineer determines the full or partial amount of the claim to which the contractor is entitled. For the determined portion of the cost during the first period of work stoppage and idling from 2004 to 2005, RMB 6,778,661.54, it was found that this referred to the specific daily statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature, as well as the monthly statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature. This indicates that for this portion of the loss, China Railway Company had already submitted a claim in accordance with the claims procedure, and the claim had been confirmed by the supervising engineer's signature. Therefore, China Railway Company's claim complied with the provisions of Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract. The trial court's judgment that Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for the loss of this determined portion was not improper and should be upheld.

As for Ruixun Company's appeal that Wang Bo, who signed the above claim materials, was not its supervising engineer and had no authority to determine claims, it was found that Wang Bo was the site supervising engineer for Section 13 of the Fuzhou Expressway project in question from May 2004 to March 2005. Article 53.5 of the General Terms of the Contract clearly stipulates that the supervising engineer has the right to determine claims. Therefore, in the absence of evidence from Ruixun Company that the endorsement by supervising engineer "Wang Bo" on the above claim basis was false, the trial court's judgment that Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for the determined portion of the losses due to work stoppage and idling, RMB 6,778,661.54, which was confirmed by supervising engineer Wang Bo's endorsement, was not improper. Ruixun Company's ground of appeal cannot be established and is not accepted by this court.

For the uncertain portion of the cost of personnel, machinery, and equipment idling during the first period of work stoppage from 2004 to 2005, RMB 6,929,833.87, it was found that this portion of the claimed amount referred to: for December 2004, the statistics table only had details for December 1 to 6, with no details for other days; for January-June 2004 and January-March 2005, there were only monthly statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature, without the corresponding daily statistics of work stoppage and idling confirmed by the site supervising engineer's signature. The above facts show that although there were monthly summary tables for this uncertain portion of losses due to work stoppage and idling, there were no daily claim endorsement statistics tables corresponding one-to-one with the summary tables. This is inconsistent with the usual practice for the determined portion of losses due to work stoppage and idling in the project in question. The trial court's decision not to support China Railway Company's claim for this uncertain portion of losses due to work stoppage and idling was not improper. China Railway Company's appeal request for Ruixun Company to compensate for this portion of the loss lacks sufficient grounds and should be dismissed.

2. On the issue of losses due to work stoppage and idling during the period from November 2006 to April 2009. Upon examination, China Railway Company also admitted that it had not made a claim for this portion of the loss in accordance with the contract. Therefore, under the circumstance that China Railway Company did not follow the claims procedure under Article 53 of the General Terms of the Contract, according to the further provisions of that article, China Railway Company is not entitled to compensation for this portion of the claimed amount. Its assertion in this case that the court should determine that Ruixun Company compensate it RMB 4 million for the losses due to work stoppage and idling has no factual or legal basis and should be dismissed.

In summary, the trial court's judgment on the amount of compensation for losses due to work stoppage and idling payable by Ruixun Company to China Railway Company was not improper. The appeal requests of both China Railway Company and Ruixun Company regarding the losses due to work stoppage and idling have no factual or legal basis and are not supported by this court.

(4) On the issue of whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for the price difference loss on raw materials and fuel oil caused by the work stoppage from March 2004 to March 2005, and if so, the amount of compensation.

In this case, China Railway Company's request for compensation from Ruixun Company for the loss in price differential of raw materials and oil products resulting from the work stoppage from March 2004 to March 2005 is based on the alleged breach of contract by Ruixun Company that caused the stoppage of the project in question. In this regard, if it is indeed true that there were wholly or partially causes attributable to Ruixun Company's breach of contract as claimed by China Railway Company, and if China Railway Company did indeed suffer losses in the price differential of raw materials and oil products due to Ruixun Company's breach, then this claim conforms to the provisions of Article 113 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, which states: "If a party fails to perform its contractual obligations, or performs them in a manner inconsistent with the agreement, thereby causing losses to the other party, the amount of damages shall be equivalent to the losses caused by the breach." Therefore, the court of first instance's examination of China Railway Company's claim in this case for compensation for the loss in price differential of raw materials and oil products resulting from the work stoppage from March 2004 to March 2005 was not improper.

Regarding the issue of whether the court of first instance correctly determined that the failure to complete the construction quantity on time for the project in question was jointly caused by China Railway Company and Ruixun Company, during the proceedings of this case, although China Railway Company appealed arguing that the work stoppage of the project in question was entirely caused by Ruixun Company's insufficient funds and incomplete land acquisition compensation, the documents from the Office of the Chief Supervision Engineer for the Fuzhou Expressway Subgrade Engineering Project (Fuzhou Chief Supervision Office Document No. (2004) 011) indicate that all construction units had problems with insufficient and mismatched machinery and equipment; the Supervision Notice for the Fuzhou Expressway Subgrade Engineering Project (No. 2004-56) states that Zhang Moumou from the Project Management Department of Contract Section 13 left the construction site from October 22 to November 14 without going through leave procedures, and was penalized with a liquidated damages of 40,000 yuan as a warning, with the expectation that the Project Management Department of Contract Section 13 strictly implement the project management system and not repeat such conduct. The above documents and notices are evidence provided by China Railway Company itself, which shows that, even based on the facts admitted by China Railway Company, there indeed existed situations where China Railway Company was ineffective in construction organization and inadequate in management. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that China Railway Company was at fault for the project delay was not improper; China Railway Company's grounds for appeal lack sufficient reasoning and are not accepted by this court. As for Ruixun Company's appeal that the work stoppage of the project in question was entirely caused by China Railway Company, based on the facts from the "Minutes of Meeting No. 253" of the Anhui Provincial Government and the fact that Anhui Expressway Company took back the right to operate and construct the Fuzhou Expressway in question, it is indeed true that Ruixun Company had insufficient funds and could not continue the project. Therefore, the court of first instance's determination that Ruixun Company was liable for the work stoppage was also proper, and Ruixun Company's appeal that the work stoppage was entirely attributable to China Railway Company is inconsistent with the facts and is not accepted by this court. As for the court of first instance's determination that the degrees of fault of both parties were equivalent and that both parties should equally bear the loss in price differential of raw materials and oil products resulting from the work stoppage from March 2004 to March 2005, this was a discretion exercised by the court of first instance based on its review of the case facts regarding the degrees of fault of the parties and the responsibilities each should bear. Neither Ruixun Company nor China Railway Company has evidence to prove that the above discretion was manifestly unfair, so this court upholds it.

As for the issue of the appraisal institution using the period from March 2005 to March 2006 as the price adjustment period for the price differential of raw materials and oil products, given that China Railway Company completed the construction quantity originally scheduled to be completed by March 2005 in March 2006, the price adjustment index adopted by the appraisal institution conforms to the provisions of Clause 70.3 of the General Conditions of the Contract, which states: "For works constructed after the extended completion date, the price adjustment calculation shall use the price index for the year of the extended completion date as the current price index." This is not improper. Furthermore, since neither China Railway Company nor Ruixun Company submitted market price information for raw materials at the construction site, the court of first instance's adoption of the price differential calculated by the appraisal institution with reference to market price information from the Hefei area was also appropriate. Therefore, Ruixun Company's grounds that the price adjustment calculation period for the price differential of raw materials and oil products and the market price information adopted in the "Expert Report" are erroneous have no factual or legal basis and are not accepted.

In summary, the court of first instance's determination that both Ruixun Company and China Railway Company were liable for causing the work stoppage and suspension of the project in question, and its judgment that Ruixun Company and China Railway Company should jointly bear the loss from this portion of the material price differential, were not improper. Both China Railway Company's and Ruixun Company's appeals requesting that the other party bear the entire loss from this portion of the price differential of raw materials and oil products lack factual and legal basis and are not supported by this court.

(5) Regarding the issue of whether Ruixun Company should compensate China Railway Company for management fees of 4,078,795 yuan.

Clause 52.3 of the General Conditions of the Contract stipulates that if, at the time of issuing the completion certificate, it is found that the contract price, after all adjustments due to the cumulative effect of changes and all adjustments made to the estimated quantities in the bill of quantities based on actual measurements, has increased or decreased by more than 15% of the "effective contract price," then the management fees of China Railway Company shall be adjusted. The above stipulation indicates that the precondition for adjusting China Railway Company's management fees is that the construction project for Contract Section 13 in question is completed, and there exists a situation where the contract price has increased or decreased after all adjustments to the contractually agreed quantities, which actually results in an increase in project management fees. Furthermore, the true intention of China Railway Company and Ruixun Company in signing this clause includes two aspects: first, the project in question is completed and a final settlement is made; second, China Railway Company actually incurred increased management fees based on the increase or decrease in quantities.

Regarding China Railway Company's claim based on the above contract clause requesting Ruixun Company to compensate for management fees of 4,078,795 yuan, on one hand, the contract in question in this case has not been fully performed; rather, during the performance of the contract, the parties mutually agreed to terminate the contract because the project in question could not continue to be completed. Therefore, the precondition in the general conditions regarding all changes in quantities after the completion of contract performance is not satisfied. Moreover, from the process of terminating the construction contract in question between the parties, China Railway Company and Ruixun Company did not have an agreement regarding the increase in management fees for the uncompleted works formed during the contract performance; on the contrary, from the terms of the "Memorandum" signed between China Railway Company and Ruixun Company, both parties agreed that this portion of losses should be handled according to the claims procedure, indicating that the claim was still in dispute and Ruixun Company had not agreed to pay this portion of the project funds. Therefore, China Railway Company's claim for management fees lacks the basis of mutual agreement between the parties. On the other hand, from the terms of the "Memorandum," both Ruixun Company and China Railway Company agreed to define this disputed portion of costs as a loss, and this loss should be a loss actually incurred by China Railway Company during the performance of the contract. However, from the facts of this case, the contract in question was not fully performed; rather, it was a liquidation of the uncompleted project under the circumstances of contract termination. China Railway Company has no evidence to prove that it actually increased management expenses under the situation where the contract was not fully performed, and thus should bear the consequences of failure to adduce evidence. Therefore, the court of first instance's failure to support China Railway Company's claim when China Railway Company did not provide evidence for its claimed increase in construction management fees of 4,078,795 yuan was not improper; China Railway Company's appeal requesting Ruixun Company to pay this portion of increased management fees should be dismissed.

(6) Regarding the issue of whether Anhui Expressway Company should bear joint and several liability for the amounts payable by Ruixun Company to China Railway Company.

First, from the contractual relationship among the parties in this case, although Anhui Expressway Company took back the investment and operation rights of the Fuzhou Expressway based on a decision of the Anhui Provincial Government, which led to the termination of the construction contract between China Railway Company and Ruixun Company, no construction contract relationship was formed between Anhui Expressway Company and China Railway Company. The employer of the project in question was Ruixun Company, and the contractor was China Railway Company, forming a contractual relationship between these two parties. Article 8 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a lawfully formed contract is legally binding on the parties. Therefore, based on the principle of privity of contract, China Railway Company should claim compensation for losses from its contractual counterpart, Ruixun Company, and cannot claim against Anhui Expressway Company, with which it has no contractual relationship. Second, from the process by which Anhui Expressway Company actually took over the expressway in question, the "Minutes of Meeting No. 253" of the Anhui Provincial Government clearly states that Anhui Expressway Company, as the new owner of the project, bears the responsibility for organizing and coordinating the new construction unit to resume work, while the original owner, Ruixun Company, bears the responsibility for handling the original construction unit and the project's previous claims. This indicates that the "Minutes of Meeting No. 253" did not require Anhui Expressway Company to assume liability for Ruixun Company's external debts. Furthermore, the Enforcement Ruling No. 19 (2010) of this court dated December 16, 2010, requires Anhui Expressway Company to assist in stopping the satisfaction of the matured debt of 30 million yuan owed to Ruixun Company. This ruling further clarifies that Anhui Expressway Company only bears the obligation to assist in execution by stopping the satisfaction of its debt to Ruixun Company, and does not assume the debts of Ruixun Company arising from the project in question. Third, from the proceedings of this case, China Railway Company has no evidence to prove the existence of statutory circumstances under which Anhui Expressway Company should bear joint and several liability with Ruixun Company. In conclusion, China Railway Company's appeal requesting Anhui Expressway Company to bear joint and several payment liability lacks both factual basis and legal basis and is not supported by this court.

Of course, if China Railway Company has evidence to prove that the compensation given to Ruixun Company by Anhui Expressway Company after taking back the construction and operation rights of the Fuzhou Expressway based on the relevant government decision is manifestly unreasonable and infringes upon its rights, it may seek resolution through other means in accordance with relevant legal provisions.

(7) Regarding the issue of whether China Railway Company's claim to have a priority right to compensation for the project in question can be established.

According to Article 3 of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on the Priority Right to Compensation for Construction Project Price: "The construction project price includes the remuneration for workers, cost of materials, and other actual expenses that the contractor should pay for the construction project, and does not include losses caused by the employer's breach of contract." The scope of rights that can exercise the priority right to compensation for construction project price does not include losses caused by the employer's breach. From the amounts claimed by China Railway Company that were supported in this case, they include two items: losses from work stoppage and suspension caused by Ruixun Company's breach, and losses from material price differential, both of which do not fall within the scope of the priority right to compensation for construction project price. Therefore, the court of first instance's failure to support China Railway Company's claim for a priority right to compensation for the project in question was not improper. China Railway Company's appeal requesting a priority right to compensation for the project in question lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

In summary, the appeal requests of both Ruixun Company and China Railway Company lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed; the judgment of first instance has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and should be upheld. In accordance with the provisions of Item 1 of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court renders the following judgment:

Appeals dismissed, and the original judgment affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee is 150,193 yuan, of which 70,168 yuan shall be borne by Anhui Ruixun Transportation Development Co., Ltd., and 80,025 yuan shall be borne by China Railway 22nd Bureau Group Co., Ltd., 4th Engineering Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
